<description>
While looking into #36759 I discovered `-notorcontrol` did the opposite of what would be expected from it and I then checked for similar issues in other init options. There are several more where `-nofoo` does something surprising including one of them crashing the node.

This PR attempts to fix all these surprising behaviors while also keeping things as simple as possible and just change behavior to something that makes sense harmless in the context of the option. Fixes that use a common approach for the fix are grouped together into a commit even if the options included themselves may have no relation at all.

| Commit | Problematic options behavior | Fix approach |
|---|---|---|
| [mempool: Reject cluster limits below 1](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/512773d111daaa4330c873ed5889b9ef511f6e3a) | `-nolimitclustercount` hits an assertion in `TxGraph` on the first mempool transaction. `-nolimitclustersize` rejects every transaction. | Reject values below 1 at startup. |
| [args: Make negation a no-op for options that are off by default](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/5d2ddcae41522a0651e20476b7481ea2e50a6fcb) | `GetArg()` returns `"0"` for a negated option. The `-no*notify` options run the command `0`, `-nosigner` uses `0` as signer, `-noi2psam` fails startup and `-norpcpassword` sets the password to `0`. Opt-in because options like `-noonion` and `-noblockfilterindex` depend on reading `"0"`. | New opt-in flag `NEGATE_TO_DEFAULT` makes `GetArg()` return the default. |
| [init: Read -cjdnsreachable and -help as booleans](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/08b4f855104b7ef25b82d66447b9e502c9bef5e9) | `-cjdnsreachable=0` and `-nocjdnsreachable` turn CJDNS on. `-nohelp` prints the help. | Use `GetBoolArg()` instead of `IsArgSet()`. |
| [args, wallet: Treat empty -blocksdir and -walletdir as unset](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/cd5bfc823063f5d06e8a15180ba05e2afc7506fb) | `-noblocksdir` writes block files relative to the working directory. `-nowalletdir` fails startup. | Fall back to the default directory, like `-datadir` does. |
| [init: Disable the automatic onion service with -notorcontrol](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/faf0a220338cbff2e045f0535635590f2d33fbe2) | `-notorcontrol` connects to `0.0.0.0:9051`, which reaches a local Tor. | Set `-listenonion=0`. |
| [init: Disallow negating options where it has no meaning](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/4b181fd471f2826659e000439f10345a483309f4) | `-nobantime`, `-nocheckblocks`, `-nomaxreceivebuffer`, `-nomaxsendbuffer` and `-nomaxtipage` read as 0, the opposite of what the user asked for. | Fail at startup with `DISALLOW_NEGATION`. |

`-nomempoolexpiry` has a similar kind of problem. It evicts transactions as soon as the next one arrives. I left it out because #36540 already is open and addresses this.
</description>

[2026-11-17] rc:4602822597 inline on src/node/mempool_args.cpp by ryanofsky (member) (edited 2026-11-17):
In commit "mempool: Reject cluster limits below 1" (512773d111daaa4330c873ed5889b9ef511f6e3a)

Note: This change looks right to me: `-nolimitclustercount` is treated as 0, and 0 is rejected as out of bounds. If we ever need an unlimited or automatic setting, an explicit value like `-limitclustercount=unlimited` would be better than a special meaning for `-nolimitclustercount`.

Also fine with me if this moves to #36861. Both reject negated and 0 values, but the [checks there](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/0ad0c71387783753356840d17d2b950367257e78/src/node/mempool_args.cpp#L37-L57) range-check before narrowing to `unsigned` and multiplying by 1000, so they also reject `-limitclustercount=4294967297`, which wraps to 1 here, and very large `-limitclustersize` values, which overflow here and crash a `-ftrapv` debug build.
[2026-11-17] rc:4602822953 inline on src/common/args.h by ryanofsky (member) (edited 2026-11-17):
In commit "args: Make negation a no-op for options that are off by default" (5d2ddcae41522a0651e20476b7481ea2e50a6fcb)

The handling of `-nosigner`, `-noi2psam`, `-norpcpassword` and the other options here looks right to me. I'd suggest renaming `NEGATE_TO_DEFAULT` to `NEGATE_TO_EMPTY` and having `GetArg()` return `""` instead of `std::nullopt`.

All of these options are read with `GetArg(name, "")`, so this doesn't change behavior now, but it matters if a default changes: if we someday enable a default signer, I2P connectivity, or RPC password, `-nosigner`, `-noi2psam` and `-norpcpassword` should still mean no signer, no I2P connections and no RPC password, not whatever the new default is. It would also be consistent with [`GetPathArg()`](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/4b181fd471f2826659e000439f10345a483309f4/src/common/args.cpp#L285), which already returns an empty path for negated options, and with the general rule in [doc/bitcoin-conf.md](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/4b181fd471f2826659e000439f10345a483309f4/doc/bitcoin-conf.md#negated-options).

And it would be a step toward the more general fix in #16545, which parses nonlegacy negated string options as `""` instead of `"0"`, and keeps the old behavior for legacy options like `-onion`.
[2026-11-17] rc:4602823246 inline on src/init.cpp by ryanofsky (member) (edited 2026-11-17):
In commit "init: Read -cjdnsreachable and -help as booleans" (08b4f855104b7ef25b82d66447b9e502c9bef5e9)

Note: The `-nocjdnsreachable` and `-nohelp` fixes look right. `IsArgSet()` returns true for negated options, so many of its current uses have this kind of bug, which makes it a footgun and something that would be great to drop.
[2026-11-17] rc:4602823499 inline on src/common/args.cpp by ryanofsky (member) (edited 2026-11-17):
In commit "args, wallet: Treat empty -blocksdir and -walletdir as unset" (cd5bfc823063f5d06e8a15180ba05e2afc7506fb)

Treating an empty `-blocksdir=` as unset looks good, but I think `-noblocksdir` should be an error instead of falling back to the default directory. `-noblocksdir` reads like an explicit instruction not to use a blocks directory, so writing blocks to the default location anyway would be misleading. `-nodatadir` is already rejected (#31212).

The simplest way to do this would be the `DISALLOW_NEGATION` flag that `-datadir` [uses](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/4b181fd471f2826659e000439f10345a483309f4/src/init.cpp#L524). A better approach in the long run would map these to `std::optional<fs::path>`, with `std::nullopt` when the option is not set and an empty path when it is negated, so code like this could return specific errors about required paths that are missing instead of generic errors about negated arguments.
[2026-11-17] rc:4602823756 inline on src/init.cpp by ryanofsky (member) (edited 2026-11-17):
re: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36880#issuecomment-6943566644

In commit "init: Disallow negating options where it has no meaning" (4b181fd471f2826659e000439f10345a483309f4)

[quoted text omitted]
I think this commit is worth keeping. These are limits where `-nofoo` reads as "no limit", but treating it as 0 means something very different: `-nocheckblocks` checks all blocks, and `-nomaxsendbuffer` pauses sending whenever anything is queued. Ideally `-nofoo` might mean unlimited for options like these, but since negation has always meant 0, an error is the safest choice.

My #36861 review recommended against more `DISALLOW_NEGATION`, but that was overbroad and I will post a correction. I still think that when 0 is just an invalid value, it's better to check for 0 so `-foo=0` and `-nofoo` get the same error, but most options here aren't like that.

The exception is `-bantime`. "No ban time" can only mean a ban time of 0, or not banning, so I think `-nobantime` should just be treated the same as `-bantime=0`, whether 0 ends up allowed or rejected (#36861 rejects it).
[2026-11-17] rc:4602824031 inline on src/wallet/walletutil.cpp by ryanofsky (member) (edited 2026-11-17):
In commit "args, wallet: Treat empty -blocksdir and -walletdir as unset" (cd5bfc823063f5d06e8a15180ba05e2afc7506fb)

I don't think `-nowalletdir` should fall back to the default wallet directory, for the same reason as `-noblocksdir` (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36880#discussion_r4602823499). For bitcoind, an error seems simplest for now. But I wouldn't rule out `-nowalletdir` and `-nodatadir` meaning what they say in the future, since they could be useful for other tools. `bitcoin-cli -nodatadir` could connect to a node without trying to read files from a datadir that may not be available, and `bitcoin-wallet -nodatadir -nowalletdir` could operate on external wallet files without touching any default wallets. Treating them as an error now keeps that possible, while treating them as the default would not.
[2026-11-17] rc:4602824369 inline on src/init.cpp by ryanofsky (member) (edited 2026-11-17):
In commit "init: Disable the automatic onion service with -notorcontrol" (faf0a220338cbff2e045f0535635590f2d33fbe2)

I think it would be safer to make `-notorcontrol` an error while `-listenonion` is enabled, asking the user to pass `-nolistenonion` if that's what they want, instead of soft-setting `-listenonion=0`. Since `-listenonion` is on by default, the error could say something like "-notorcontrol requires -nolistenonion" rather than mention `-listenonion=1`.

`-torcontrol` is only used for the onion service now, but it could be used for other things later, so it's useful to know whether the user wants to disable onion listening or everything that uses the control port. An error also helps users who don't know what the control port is used for.

That said, this is more borderline than the other cases, since "no" here really does mean none, so keeping the soft-set as a convenience seems ok too. But then `-torcontrol=0` should behave the same way, like `-proxy=0`, `-onion=0` and `-connect=0`, which already treat 0 as disabled. Currently it still connects to `0.0.0.0:9051`, since it isn't a negated value.
[2026-11-17] r:5942750123 review COMMENTED by ryanofsky (member) (edited 2026-11-17):
Concept ACK 4b181fd471f2826659e000439f10345a483309f4, and approach ACK with a few tweaks.

My main feedback is that I think "no" should mean none, false, or zero, or else be an error. We should avoid more clever interpretations like "default" or "unlimited", even where they could be sensible, because the precedent for mapping negated options to falsy values is well established, and other interpretations create unnecessary ambiguity.

Inline comments suggest changes to `NEGATE_TO_DEFAULT` (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36880#discussion_r4602822953), `-noblocksdir`/`-nowalletdir` (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36880#discussion_r4602823499, https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36880#discussion_r4602824031), `-notorcontrol` (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36880#discussion_r4602824369) and `-nobantime` (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36880#discussion_r4602823756).
